name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.135.0 — The mocks seed now names the client's real records and the two dense screens the theme pick judges every candidate on (ADR-0013): the seed's `## Records` section names one JSON file of at least three real records per entity, refused missing/short/invented at seed-done (and on a cold host the refusal still names the remedy with a literal `<entity>` placeholder); `## Dense screens` accepts one or two declared labels (the singular `## Dense screen` heading still parses for hosts seeded earlier); and journey-drawn now warns per screen and refuses per journey when no drawn screen carries a value from those records, so a journey never reaches the client on placeholder data. 7.134.0 — The /spec:status default screen now carries every startable lane in its 🎯 Next block — escape entries first, then the parallel-lane fan-out with its merge-conflict heads-up, or a single pick marked 🚦 solo — so no runnable work is reachable only by typing --all. The 📋 All open work header is deleted; --all now adds only what you cannot start yet (🕓 after that, ⛔ blocked, placed under Next and ahead of the decide lines) plus the hygiene catalogue, and never re-prints the top pick. The footer drops its parallel count and reads · {n} more open / · nothing else open. A queued free-text item renders as its one-line id-led row on the default screen too. --next, --json, --pretty and --brief are byte-for-byte unchanged. 7.133.0 — Every seed journey edge is now a real, clickable control: the authoring session marks the element that leads to the next screen with data-to="<label>", journey-drawn refuses any seed edge with no such control or a data-to naming an undeclared screen (lib/mock-seed-checks.js's edgeGaps), and a mock served with ?walk injects walk-mode.browser.js so a click inside the frame reports where it went — to a declared screen or a miss — to the page that embeds it, the mechanism spec 03's journey player reads.
